## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Where we are in 2022
• Spring 2020 Testing
• USED granted testing waivers in 2020 due to the onset of the pandemic in
March 2020.
• IL tested approximately 80,000 students in 2020 prior to the onset of the
pandemic.
• Besides those students, all other testing was cancelled in 2020.
• No growth analyses were conducted due to the cancellation of testing in 2020

Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Where we are in 2022
• Spring 2021 Testing
• Accountability waivers were granted for states but testing waivers were not universally
granted.
• The New Meridian consortium was broadly impacted by testing changes:
• DC was given a waiver to not test in 2021.
• NJ tested using an abbreviated form (Start Strong) in Fall 2021
• IL tested in spring 2021 and offered Fall 2021 testing
• BIE and DoDEA testing in spring 2021.
• States that tested did not see test participation at levels normally observed (i.e., 95%).
USED granted testing waivers in 2020 due to the onset of the pandemic in March 2020.
• Illinois (and New Meridian) conducted skip-year/gap year growth analyses from 2019 to
• Academic impact results from these analyses were presented to the TAC in December,
Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Where we are in 2022
• Illinois conducted consecutive year growth analyses from 2021 to 2022.
• In 2022, four types of SGP analyses were conducted for Illinois data:
• Cohort referenced analyses: These analyses create growth norms from the 2021 to 2022
students. These growth norms yield cohort means/median SGPs of 50 and obscure COVID-19
academic impact. Both SIMEX (measurement error corrected) and non-SIMEX SGPs are
calculated.
• Baseline referenced analyses: Historical, consecutive-year growth norms were created using
2018 to 2019 data. These growth growth analyses don’t have mean/median SGPs of 50 and
can be used to investigate overall COVID-19 academic impact. Both SIMEX (measurement
error corrected) and non-SIMEX SGPs are calculated.
• All analyses were single prior analyses.
• Projections (lagged and straight) were calculated for 2022 data using baseline
growth norms in case they were needed.

Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">SGP Summary of Cohort versus Baseline Referenced
• Cohort referenced SGPs
• Growth norms created from the current cohort of students.
• Typical way that SGPs are calculated.
• Both consortium and state referenced norms are created.
• Mean/median will by 50 for all grade x content area analyses.
• Cannot investigate overall impact of the pandemic on students.
• Can investigate differential impact of the pandemic on students.
• Does not require scale stability across years.
• Baseline referenced SGPs.
• Growth norms created from historical (i.e., pre-COVID) cohorts of students.
• Mean/median 50 for historical cohort, not necessarily 50 for current cohort.
• Both consortium and state referenced baseline norms are created (using 2019 membership)
• Extent of deviation from (i.e. below) 50 is indicative of less learning/pandemic related academic impact.
• Mean SGP deviation of 5 corresponds to an effect size of 0.18.
• Can investigate BOTH overall impact and differential impact
• Requires scale stability across years.
Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/06.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">SGP Calculations
• SGP calculations were performed using the SGP package and R software
environment based upon data supplied by Pearson.
• To facilitate the calculation of baseline SGPs across multiple states, we
created an additional R package, SGPmatrices, that contains all baseline
matrices for states/organizations.
• SGPmatrices
• Source code associated with calculations are available on GitHub (private
account):
• Illinois GitHub Repo
• Analyses were conducted first by state/organization based upon availability
of data provided by Pearson and then at the consortium level once all data
was available.
Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/07.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">SGP Calculations 2022
• SGP analyses were successfully conducted in July with data provided by
Pearson.
• No analytic issues were encountered as part of the analyses and data
was returned.
• Cohort referenced analyses all displayed good model fit.

Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/08.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">SGP Analyses and Academic Impact &amp; Recovery
• Impact is synonymous with deceleration.
• Recovery is synonymous with acceleration.
• The pandemic, functioning as an academic “headwind” through
all the edu-disruptions slows the rate of learning of students (i.e.,
deceleration).
• Decreased rates of learning lead to lower attainment for students.
• Growth and status changes are opposite sides of the same coin.
However, status changes are much more sensitive to population
changes (e.g., non-participation) than growth.
Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/09.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Student Attainment and Growth (SGP) Results
• The following slides show Illinois student attainment and growth
results for 2022.
• Results presented do not include any exclusion rules IDOE may apply
for accountability purposes (e.g., full-academic year enrollment)
• We report both cohort &amp; baseline referenced SGPs in these slides
• Cohort referenced results fail to show overall impact.
• Due to the highly skewed nature of the SGP results, we recommend median
SGP over mean SGP in this instance.
• We also provide 2019 and 2021 results to understand pandemic
related academic impact/recovery
Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/13.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Points of Clarification for Status Results
• Decrease in attainment (as a decrease in percent proficient) between
2019 and 2021 is the most often reported statistic related to state testing
in 2021.
• This analysis &amp; statistic (percent proficient) are problematic for several
reasons:
• Using 2019 as a counterfactual for where students would have been had
the pandemic not occurred is problematic for several reasons including:
• Changes in student cohort composition is not accounted for.
• Improvement between 2019 and 2021 that would have occurred is not
accounted for.
• Missing data in 2021 not accounted for.
• Multiple imputation results imply results would have been lower in 2021 had all
students tested.
Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/14.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Points of Clarification for Status Results

• Effect sizes associated with decreases range from approximately 0.15 to 0.4.
• Participation rates (derived from decreases in observed test scores between
2019 and 2021) vary by grade and state/organization but suggest
participation between 60% and 80% (mostly toward the lower end)
• In general, the achievement decreases observed are large and are consistent
with large academic impact.
• Other states, with and without missing data, show similar decreases.
• In general, current results based upon incomplete data likely represent a best-
case scenario compared to what would appear given fuller participation.

Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/17.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Discussion
• Status and growth analyses from 2019 to 2021 indicated large academic impact
associated with the pandemic on students across all grade levels and content areas.
• Status and growth analyses from 2021 to 2022 indicate (on average) a return to
normal rates of learning.
• NOTE: It is important to distinguish between the system returning to normal and
the students in the system returning to normal.
• The system itself can return to normal rates of learning without the students
in the system catching-up to where they would have been.
• Eventually, students impacted will leave the system, possibly without ever
having caught up to where they would have been.
• To help interpret and communicate results across various grades, content areas
subgroups and states, we built custom graphics classes in R for visualization
purposes.
Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/28.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">SGP Analysis Plans post 2022
• Continued use of the current assessment allows Illinois to compare student
growth and attainment to pre-COVID times.
• Important to distinguish between system level recovery and student level
recovery.
• Growth and status analyses will continue to be valuable assets in understanding
the extent to which students are recovering from pandemic related academic
impact.

Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/29.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Summary of Findings
• SGP analyses were successfully conducted for Illinois in Spring 2022
• Cohort and baseline referenced SGPs were calculated.
• Baseline referenced analyses suggest, on average, that students in the
Illinois education system have returned to typical rates of learning.
• However, typical rates of learning are not sufficient to catch students up
to where they would have been.
• Average, of course, mask important variation with some students
demonstrating robust recovery and other demonstrating further
declines.

Illinois TAC 12/2/2021</div>
```
